reason: Exact: 'petiole wing' is already a listed synonym of PO_0025129 petiole lamina (a flattened, leaf-like outgrowth along the petiole). The grounding failure is probably in how the compound word is matched, not a missing class.
Exact: 'resin duct' is a listed synonym of PO_0005665 resin canal. 'with 2 short resin ducts' and 'resin ducts 1-3' are counts (pattern 03).

Narrower: the hard middle layer of the testa in gymnosperm seeds (cycads, Ginkgo, Gnetum). PO has no layer classes for the testa and only one flora uses the word, so it maps to testa and loses the layer. A sclerotesta/sarcotesta pair could go to PO upstream if more gymnosperm floras need it.

In Inga and related mimosoids, the stemonozone is the thickened zone at the base where the corolla and the staminal tube are joined. Expressed as the base of the staminal tube. Specialist word from one flora; the corolla share of the zone is lost.
Exact: in grasses an anthecium is the floret (lemma, palea and the flower). 'spikelet with 2 to 3 anthecia' is a count of florets with the spikelet (PO_0009051) as container (pattern 03).
Exact: the pericarp is always part of a fruit, so 'fruit' adds nothing.

target: calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005), whole: calyx (PO_0009060) at fruit development stage (PO_0001002)
reason: Lobe of the calyx as it is in fruit (persistent, often enlarged). Calyx lobe exists; 'fruiting' already has a reviewed reading as fruit development stage (flora_context_words.tsv), so this is pattern 12 or 06.
Narrower: the peltate (scutiform) ovule-bearing unit of a cycad female cone, which floras call a megasporophyll; PO_0009027 lists macrosporophyll and cone scale as synonyms.

target: count of sporangium (PO_0025094) with container sorus (PO_0025359)
reason: A fragment: 'per sorus' (por soro), badly stemmed. It is the container phrase of a count: 'sporangia 6-36 per sorus' counts sporangia (PO_0025094) with sorus (PO_0025359) as container (pattern 03 / 14).

Narrower: in Cactaceae the pericarpel is the receptacle (stem) tissue around the inferior ovary, often carrying areoles ('unarmed', 'areoles immersed'). The nearest PO class is receptacle; hypanthium (PO_0009065) is the floral tube above it. Only one flora uses it; if Cactaceae floras need it more widely, propose it to PO upstream as part of the receptacle.

synonyms: free part of the staminal tube
reason: The part of the staminal tube above where it is joined to the corolla, i.e. its distal region; bearer is the staminal tube with the upper-part region.
Exact: tertiary nerve = third-order leaf vein, PO_0008021 (synonym 'third order leaf vein').

target: bladder trap (FLOPO_0986084), its mouth; position quality (basal/lateral/terminal)
reason: In Utricularia (utrículo = trap), the position of the trap mouth (basal, lateral, terminal) is a standard key character. Bearer is the bladder trap; the position of its opening is pattern 18. Not the Carex utricle: a perigynium has a beak, not a positioned opening.
Exact: a vascular cylinder is a stele (PO uses 'root vascular cylinder' as a synonym of root stele). 'one central, one or more peripheral' counts steles (pattern 03/14).
A style in a female flower: pattern 12. 'female' has a reviewed reading for flower in flora_context_words.tsv; pistillate flower PO_0025599 can also serve as a fixed container.

target: leaf lamina (PO_0020039), whole: vascular leaf (PO_0009025) + fertile (PATO_0000955)

A pedicel in a pistillate flower: pattern 12. 'pistillate' has a reviewed reading as female for flower.
Apex region of the seed; PO has no seed apex class, and the patterns express it as seed + apex region. Rounded/acute/mucronate are apex shapes.

A mistranslation of 'ramo estigmático' (stigmatic branch). 'Shoot' is wrong; it is the stigma-bearing branch of the style, 'bifid' or 'simple'. Exact for style branch; stigma lobe (FLOPO_0986009) is the alternative where the branches are lobes of the stigma itself.

A general small point that needs the organ it belongs to. Same decision as for apiculus, apiculum, apicula and mucro in flora_rejected_bearer_words.tsv. Where the organ is named, read it as that organ + apiculate, with the length as a length of the organ's apex. PO has apiculus classes only for the palea (PO_0006033) and the lemma (PO_0025616).

reason: Blade of the leaves on side branches as opposed to the main stem: a part of a qualified or positioned whole (pattern 12/18). The sizes are in cm, so these are vascular leaves, not moss branch leaves.
Apex region of the capsule; there is no PO fruit apex class. 'Beaked' could instead use fruit beak (FLOPO_0986139).

Cells on the dorsal side of some unnamed organ (a bryophyte leaf, an indusium, a trap?). 'fragile', 'inflated' and sizes in µm don't settle which organ, and there are no FLOPO cell classes for a dorsal position. Needs context.

target: plant fiber cell (PO_0025407) with container endocarp (PO_0009086)
reason: Fibres of or on the endocarp, as in palms: a part with a fixed whole (pattern 12 fixed-container note). In palm floras these are fibre strands rather than single cells, but PO 'plant fiber' is the nearest.
Narrower: the stalk carrying a pair of flowers (paired-flowered cymes, e.g. Lonicera) is the peduncle of a two-flowered inflorescence.
Blade of the lateral (not terminal) leaflets. 'lateral' has a reviewed series-position reading for leaflet in flora_context_words.tsv: pattern 12/18.

A coloured zone (spot or line) on a tepal, petal or corolla throat; which organ carries it is often not stated ('above claws'). In line with 'eye', rejected as unclear in flora_rejected_bearer_words.tsv. Where the organ is named, read the colour as a colour of that organ. A PO class (part of the perianth) could be proposed if several floras need it.
Exact: a nectar-secreting gland is a nectary. Use flower nectary (PO_0009056) where it is in the flower.
Exact: PO_0025266 plant ovary locule. 'à 5 loges' is a count with the ovary as container.
The opening at the top of a tubular perianth. Expressed as the apex of the perianth tube, like corolla throat (FLOPO_0986110) for the corolla. 'contracted', 'ciliate' and 'lobate' describe that rim.
